quote: Theorem 3.1. Let Xλ1, Xλ2 (Xλ∗1, Xλ∗2) be independent non-negative random variables with Xλi ~ TG(λi) (Xλ∗i ~ TG(λ∗i)), i = 1, 2. Further, suppose that Ip1, Ip2 (Ip∗1, Ip∗2) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xλi's (Xλ∗i's), with E[Ipi] = pi (E[Ip∗i] = p∗i), i = 1, 2. Let h : [0, 1] → I ⊂ R+ be a differentiable and strictly increasing concave function on [0, 1] with the non-zero derivative. Then for (λ, h(p)) ∈ S2, we have (λ∗1 λ∗2; h(p∗1) h(p∗2)) ≪ (λ1 λ2; h(p1) h(p2)) ⟹ Y2:2 ≤st Y∗2:2.

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let Xλ1, . . . , Xλn (Xλ∗1, . . . , Xλ∗n) be independent non-negative random variables with Xλi ~ TG(λi) (Xλ∗i ~ TG(λ∗i)), i = 1, . . . , n. Further, suppose that Ip1, . . . , Ipn (Ip∗1, . . . , Ip∗n) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xλi's (Xλ∗i's), with E[Ipi] = pi (E[Ip∗i] = p∗i), i = 1, . . . , n. Let h : [0, 1] → I ⊂ R+ be a differentiable and strictly increasing concave function on [0, 1], with non-zero derivative. Then for (λ, h(p)) ∈ Sn, we have (λ∗1 ... λ∗n; h(p∗1) ... h(p∗n)) = (λ1 ... λn; h(p1) ... h(pn)) Tω ⟹ Yn:n ≤st Y∗n:n.

quote: Let Xλ1, Xλ2, Xλ3 (Xλ∗1, Xλ∗2, Xλ∗3) be independent random variables with Xλi ~ TE(λi, 0.5) (Xλ∗i ~ TE(λ∗i, 0.5)), i = 1, 2, 3. Also, suppose that (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (−0.7, 0.8, −0.9), (λ∗1, λ∗2, λ∗3) = (−0.1806, 0.0896, −0.7090), (p1, p2, p3) = (0.4, 0.2, 0.7), and (p∗1, p∗2, p∗3) = (0.4345, 0.3698, 0.4711).
